title: ～と聞いた — I heard that ～
summary: Passes on information you heard from someone: “I heard that ～.” It attaches to the plain form of a sentence. The speaker is the one who heard it, so it is used for hearsay you received personally.

patterns.form: 普通形 ＋ と聞いた／と聞きました
patterns.gloss: plain form + と聞いた (polite: と聞きました)

body.p: 聞く (to hear) is in the past because the hearing already happened. The part before と is what you heard, in plain form: テストがある (there is a test), 引っ越す (will move). The source can be added with から or に: 先生から聞いた.

～そうだ also reports hearsay and is common in writing. ～と言われている is general hearsay without a personal source. ～と聞いた is natural in conversation when you want to say who or what your information came from.

examples.ja: 来週（らいしゅう）テストがあると聞（き）きました。
examples.romaji: Raishū tesuto ga aru to kikimashita.
examples.tr: I heard there is a test next week.

examples.ja: 駅前（えきまえ）に新（あたら）しい店（みせ）ができると聞（き）いた。
examples.romaji: Ekimae ni atarashii mise ga dekiru to kiita.
examples.tr: I heard that a new shop is opening in front of the station.

examples.ja: 隣（となり）の人（ひと）が来月（らいげつ）引（ひ）っ越（こ）すと聞（き）きました。
examples.romaji: Tonari no hito ga raigetsu hikkosu to kikimashita.
examples.tr: I heard that my neighbor is moving away next month.

pitfalls: Use the plain form before と, even in a polite sentence: あると聞きました, not ありますと聞きました.
The verb is normally past (聞いた). 聞く in the present means “I ask / I will ask”.
